images.shows: Plain French/Italian secretary-hand letter, Alberto Pio de Carpi to the Cardinal de Sens (Antoine Duprat), Rome, 18 May 1520 -- matches the finding aid's folio 16 item exactly. No cipher of any kind on this leaf, confirming the finding aid's own wording (no 'en chiffres' note for this item).

images.shows: SUPERSEDED CHARACTERISATION, kept for the record: this sweep's low-resolution view read the tail as an 'arithmetic-numeral cipher'. Full-resolution imaging on 23 Sept 2026 (see below) shows it is instead a symbol/glyph substitution alphabet, and that it continues far past this leaf. See ciphertext.txt for the corrected reading.

images_added_23_sept_2026_transcription_.shows: Folio 20 recto (period ink foliation confirmed, docket 'C. Carpi 1526'): Alberto Pio de Carpi to Madame [Louise de Savoie]. About 20 lines plain French, then 9 lines of cipher (rows 3-11) ending abruptly at the foot of the page with no closing -- the letter continues onto the verso (see f24 below). Transcribed in ciphertext.txt (single pass, see reconciliation.md).

ONE photographed opening = folio 20 VERSO (left page: 22 lines cipher, then 2 plain paragraphs) + folio 21 RECTO (right page, period foliation '21' visible top right: 13 more cipher lines, then 2 plain closing paragraphs, date 'Rome ce xxvij [27] jour d'Octobre l'an mil Vc xxv [1525]', signed 'de Carpi'). This is the letter's actual ending; item 20 therefore spans 3 page-sides, not 1 (see ciphertext.txt header for the full correction and the date discrepancy against the finding aid's '22 oct.'). NOT transcribed past folio 20 recto this session; crops saved in crops/ for a follow-up pass.

Next opening after f24: folio 21 VERSO (left page, address panel with a wax-seal hole and mirror show-through of the letter's own last lines -- the outer wrapper of the folded letter, blank apart from the address) + a blank facing page. Confirms the letter's true close is on folio 21 recto (f24-right), not here; no further cipher.

images_added_23_sept_2026_transcription_.shows: Folio 28 recto (period foliation '28' visible top right): Nicolas Raince to Madame [Louise de Savoie], opens 'Madame, pour ce que par les depesches de monseigneur le conte...', 2 plain paragraphs, then ~15 lines cipher in the SAME alphabet as folio 20/21 (confirmed by eye, including a shared rare 'three small boxes' mark -- see ciphertext_f28.txt). This is check-solved's item 28.
Folio 28 verso + folio 29 recto, one opening, BOTH PAGES entirely in cipher (no plain text at all), roughly 30 lines per page. Not transcribed; see ciphertext_f28.txt for extent and why.

Folio 29 verso (6 more cipher lines, then plain) + folio 30 recto (plain, closing 'Madame' paragraphs, date 'de Rome ce xxv[e] jour Doctobre l'an mil Vc xxv' [25 Oct 1525], signed 'Nicolas Raince' -- matches the finding aid's item 28 exactly).

note: Canvas-to-folio offset in this volume grows through the early gathering (canvas16=folio16, offset0; canvas21=folio19, offset+2; canvas23=folio20, offset+3; f34=folio28, offset+6) and is NOT linear -- extra unfoliated address/wrapper leaves are inserted irregularly (confirmed: f25 is folio 21's own wrapper, a leaf with no foliation of its own). Do not extrapolate folio position from a fixed per-canvas offset; read the period ink foliation (small numeral, top right of most rectos) directly from a full-resolution fetch instead. Folio 28 (Raince to Madame, item 28) is now located and characterised (f34-f36, see above) -- the 20 Sept sweep's 'not located' note for it is superseded. The four 1535 'Dechiffrement' leaves (ff.56, 60, 72, 76) were NOT located in this pass: canvases sampled at reduced width without success were f58, f60, f62, f64, f66, f68, f70, f72, f74, f76, f78 (a period annotation resembling 'Segrement'/cipher-related marginalia was seen near f64 but not confirmed as one of the four items); a denser bracket or the reading-room folio-search box would be needed next.
